title: Rushmire Hill Geotechnical Remediation and Standish Multi-User Path
description:
This advert is intended to notify potential suppliers of the combined tender including both the Rushmire Hill Geotechnical remediation and the Standish Multi-User Path works. These two pieces of work have been packaged as a single tender.\r
\r
Rushmire Hill Geotechnical Remediation\r
Rushmire Hill is in South Gloucestershire, near Wotton-under-Edge, approximately 1.2 km south of Cotswold Edge Golf Course. The works are required to stabilise the B4058 carriageway, which has historically suffered deterioration from ground movement. Remediation works will include sheet piling along the GCC owned verge, verge and carriageway reconstruction. Site clearance will also be required to facilitate the piling works. \r
\r
Summary of Construction Phase key deliverables are as follows:\r
Site clearance including tree clearance over approx. 255m, 3.5m width.\r
Sheet piling installation along an approx. 255m length of verge.\r
Partial carriageway reconstruction of the northbound carriageway over 280m. \r
Carriageway resurfacing over approx. 300m\r
Ground investigation including the installation of 3 no. inclinometers and 1 no. slotted standpipe in the carriageway\r
Traffic Management during the construction works.\r
Maintain residents' access during the construction works.\r
\r
Standish Multi User Path\r
The works are located between the Horsemarling Lane roundabout and Blackbridge access track to the south of Standish, Gloucestershire. This scheme is part of a wider strategic scheme to boost active travel provision within the county, through the creation of the Gloucestershire Cycle Spine and includes a section of bridle way. \r
\r
Summary of Construction Phase key deliverables are as follows:\r
Construction of 400m of 3m wide new shared use path and bridal way\r
150m of carriageway realignment and works to splinter island\r
Streetlighting column installation and relocation. Columns will be supplied by GCC.\r
Utility diversion works (pre-arranged by GCC for Principal Contractor to liaise/accommodate).\r
Drainage works that tie-in to existing systems and includes ditch and attenuation pond construction.\r
Traffic Management during the construction works.\r
Maintain residents' access during the construction works\r
\r
Gloucestershire County Council are seeking a Principal Contractor to deliver the construction phase of this project.\r
\r
A summary of the outline programme for the combined packages of works is shown below:\r
Tender period: 26th Sep - 31st Oct 2024\r
Award: Monday 25th November 2024\r
Anticipated Works Start Date: Monday 6th January 2025\r
Completion: Friday 30th May 2025 \r
Overall Duration: 22 weeks\r
Indicative Value: (£2.2M + £0.44M VAT) = £2.64M\r
\r
The proposed procurement route will be a single stage (Open Procedure) using the NEC4 ECC form of Contract, Option A Priced Contract with Activity Schedule.\r
\r
Full details will be available in the tender pack advertised on Procontract Thursday 26th September 2024.\r
\r

title: Weather Forecaster Provision for Gloucestershire Highways
description:
Gloucestershire County Council (GCC) are seeking an established and recognised weather forecasting company with appropriate skills and resource available to undertake  winter highways weather forecasting services. \r
The Tender Process seeks to determine the most economically advantageous Tender for the Authority. This will be a compliant and sustainable (i.e. not "abnormally low") bid with an overall score higher than any other Bidder's overall score.\r
\r
Specification\r
Forecast Service: Domain based forecasting service. Forecast text written specifically for the geographic area managed by GCC (for the avoidance of doubt this means a more generic regional text shall not be provided)\r
All elements of information provided to GCC shall be consistent - for example, hazard tables with the text forecast will be consistent with the textual element.\r
Morning Summary Text - to be provided at 9am to ensure it includes the coldest period predicted by previous lunchtime and evening update forecasts.\r
24 hour Domain Forecast for 3 areas within the county (East = Cotswold District, Central = Stroud District, Gloucester and Cheltenham and Tewkesbury Borough, West = Forest of Dean District)\r
24-hour Site Specific Forecast Graphs for our weather sensors (currently 11 but looking at additional sites as part of our County Weather Station Strategy)\r
2-5 Day Forecast is the minimum service level 2-8 day forecast is desirable with options for 6-10day summary\r
Weather radar for the UK indicating short and medium-term precipitation type and intensity\r
Consultancy\r
Monitoring and Alerting\r
Web Portal\r
Forecast delivery methods\r
Management and Reporting\r
\r
Contract term is for 2 years with the option to extend by a further 2 years to a total of 4 years. Extension will be dependent on successful performance of the contract.\r
\r
Anticipated value is £20k per annum, total contract value is £96k (4 x £20k + VAT of £16k).\r
\r
Full details are available in the ITT documents available on Procontract https://procontract.due-north.com/Advert?advertId=34aed741-1d3d-ee11-8124-005056b64545

title: Invitation to Tender for Willersey Evaluation - AWARD
description:
Historic England are looking for a partner to explore (through targeted excavation) the context of two Roman cavalry swords discovered during a metal detecting rally near Broadway in Gloucestershire.  Historic England geophysical survey showed the find spot sits within a complex of buried archaeological remains including later prehistoric or Roman settlement. 
      Though the find is public knowledge, reference to the exact location in outreach material should be avoided until after the site has been assessed, and statutory protection afforded if justified.
      We wish to collaborate with an experienced archaeological services organisation who will provide site staff, an excavation co-director, finds and environmental processing expertise, and a digital recording system in use or in development.  They should be based as near the site as possible, with demonstrable knowledge of the local archaeological landscape and preferably also connections/experience with local community groups. Proximity to the sight is crucial for Net Zero targets, and to enable safe and efficient transfer of finds/ecofacts/samples to storage on a regular basis
